sidebarDescription: Reduce editor friction by learning four repeatable VS Code workflows: navigate, manipulate, run or debug deliberately, and recover through the Command Palette.
connection: Session 01 created a multi-project solution containing App, Domain, Infrastructure, Web, ScratchPad, and Tests. Before Session 02 begins moving among those projects, this optional sidebar separates C# difficulty from editor-state friction.
objectives: Use a small set of high-value commands to navigate files, symbols, definitions, and editing positions.
Control common editor UI state without depending on the mouse.
Explain why F5 does not simply run the file currently visible in a multi-project solution.
Deliberately select a Run and Debug project or use an explicit dotnet command.
Use the Command Palette as the primary recovery and command-discovery tool.
Read a dense generic IntelliSense signature one parameter at a time instead of memorizing it.

visuals.title: Navigate by intent
visuals.explanation: Open a file by name, find a symbol, visit its definition, and return. These actions are more reusable than memorizing where every file sits in the Explorer.

visuals.title: Manipulate editor state
visuals.explanation: The sidebar, terminal, bottom panel, and editor groups are views you can show, hide, split, focus, and restore without changing project files.

visuals.title: Run and Debug have targets
visuals.explanation: In a multi-project solution, the visible file and selected debug target are separate state. F5 follows the selected configuration, not your gaze.

visuals.title: Recover through the Command Palette
visuals.explanation: When a shortcut is forgotten, intercepted by RDP, or hidden behind confusing UI state, Ctrl+Shift+P lets you search for the action by name.

preQuiz.prompt: You forgot the shortcut for splitting an editor. What is the best general fallback?
options: Open the Command Palette and search for split editor
preQuiz.explanation: The Command Palette lets you find and run commands by intent without memorizing every binding.

preQuiz.prompt: In a solution containing App and ScratchPad, what does F5 debug?
options: The currently selected launch or project configuration
preQuiz.explanation: VS Code remembers debugging state. The active editor does not necessarily determine the debug target.

preQuiz.prompt: Which approach most explicitly identifies the console project you intend to run?
options: dotnet run --project followed by its .csproj path
preQuiz.explanation: An explicit project path avoids ambiguity about which executable project should run.

concept.title: The main lesson: memorize less, recover better
paragraphs: You do not need to memorize every VS Code shortcut. Learn a small set of high-value navigation commands, understand that VS Code remembers UI and debugging state, and use Ctrl+Shift+P to discover or execute everything else.
This course already provides a searchable Shortcuts widget on session pages. Use that widget as a reference; use this sidebar to practice workflows and understand how commands work together.
concept.code: Ctrl+Shift+P  →  type what you want to do  →  choose the command

concept.title: 1. Navigate
paragraphs: Navigation commands answer different questions: Which file? Which symbol? Where is this defined? Where was I before? Word-boundary movement handles small movements inside one line.
Use Ctrl+P and type part of a filename instead of expanding folders repeatedly. In Quick Open, @ searches symbols in the selected file; Ctrl+Shift+O opens that symbol search directly.

rows: Type part of Program.cs, Class1.cs, or a project filename
Find a symbol in this file
Jump to a class, method, or member
Find a symbol in the workspace
Visit the declaration behind a type or member
Return after visiting another file or definition
Move through an identifier or statement without the mouse
Expand a selection by meaningful text boundaries

concept.title: 2. Manipulate
paragraphs: Editor layout is temporary UI state. Splitting an editor does not copy a file, and hiding a panel does not delete anything. Treat layout commands as reversible tools.
Shortcut bindings can vary by keyboard, extension, operating system, or remote environment. If a binding fails, search for the command name in Ctrl+Shift+P.

rows: View: Toggle Primary Side Bar Visibility
Show or hide the bottom panel

concept.title: 3. Run / Debug
paragraphs: Run means execute the program. Debug means execute it with a debugger attached so breakpoints can pause the program and expose its state. Run Without Debugging and Start Debugging are related but different actions.

In this solution, App, ScratchPad, Tests, and Web are different runnable or testable targets. F5 does not mean run the code I am looking at. It uses the launch or project configuration currently selected in Run and Debug, and VS Code may remember a selection from earlier work.

Open Run and Debug with Ctrl+Shift+D and deliberately inspect the selected target before using F5. If a test or run dropdown behaves inconsistently, do not trust it blindly: reselect the target or use an explicit terminal command.

rows: Inspect and select the intended project/configuration
Run the selected target with the debugger attached
Run the selected target without breakpoint debugging
Pause when execution reaches the selected executable line
Execute the current line without entering called methods
Name the target directly instead of relying on remembered editor state

concept.title: 4. Recover
paragraphs: Ctrl+Shift+P is the main fallback when you forget a shortcut, have too many commands to memorize, or are connected through RDP and a key combination does not reach VS Code reliably.

Search by intent: toggle terminal, single column, format document, select debug configuration, or reload window. The Command Palette also shows the shortcut currently assigned in your installation, when one exists.
Recovery is a normal workflow skill. A missing panel, unexpected split, or stale debug selection is usually reversible editor state—not damaged source code.
concept.code:
Ctrl+Shift+P
Search: View: Single Column
Search: View: Toggle Terminal
Search: Format Document
Search: Debug: Select and Start Debugging
Search: Developer: Reload Window

lab.objective: Practice four VS Code workflows in the completed Session 01 solution without changing application behavior.
lab.startingCondition: Complete Session 01 first and open the solution root in VS Code. The generated template files are enough for this optional exercise; no new C# concept or permanent source change is required.

labs.title: Navigate Without Hunting Through Folders
labs.objective: Move among files, symbols, definitions, and editing positions using intent-based navigation.
labs.task: Open generated files by name, visit a symbol or definition, return to the starting location, and manipulate a selection without using the mouse.
instructions: Press Ctrl+P.
Type part of PinkMachine19.TimeClock.ScratchPad/Program.cs.
Open the ScratchPad Program.cs result.
Press Ctrl+P again.
Open Class1.cs from the Domain project.
Press Ctrl+Shift+O.
Select the Class1 symbol if it appears in the symbol list.
Return to ScratchPad/Program.cs with Ctrl+Tab.
Place the cursor on Console.
Press F12 to visit its definition or metadata.
Press Alt+Left to return to Program.cs.
Move across the template output statement with Ctrl+Left and Ctrl+Right.
Select one word with Ctrl+Shift+Right.
Press Escape to clear the selection without editing the file.

labs.title: Manipulate and Restore the Workspace
labs.objective: Treat panels and editor groups as reversible UI state rather than something that requires mouse-driven repair.
labs.task: Hide and restore common views, compare two Program.cs files side by side, format a document, and return to one editor group.
instructions: Press Ctrl+B to hide the sidebar.
Press Ctrl+B again to restore the sidebar.
Press Ctrl+` to open the integrated terminal.
Open App/Program.cs with Ctrl+P.
Press Ctrl+\ to split the active editor.
Open ScratchPad/Program.cs in the second editor group with Ctrl+P.
Use Ctrl+1 and Ctrl+2 to move focus between the editor groups.
Press Shift+Alt+F to format the active Program.cs.
Press Alt+Shift+1 to restore a single editor group.
If any shortcut fails, use Ctrl+Shift+P to run the equivalent command by name.

labs.title: Choose the Run or Debug Target Deliberately
labs.objective: Separate the visible editor from VS Code's remembered execution target and practice one breakpoint-driven debugging cycle.
labs.task: Run ScratchPad explicitly, select ScratchPad in Run and Debug, pause on its template output, and verify that F5 follows the selected target rather than the visible file.
instructions: Open the integrated terminal at the solution root.

instructions.text: Run ScratchPad by naming its project explicitly.

instructions: Confirm that the ScratchPad template output appears.
Press Ctrl+Shift+D to open Run and Debug.
Inspect the currently selected launch or project configuration.
Select PinkMachine19.TimeClock.ScratchPad deliberately.
Open ScratchPad/Program.cs.
Place the cursor on its Console.WriteLine statement.
Press F9 to add a breakpoint.
Press F5 to start debugging the selected target.
Confirm that execution pauses on the ScratchPad breakpoint.
Press F10 once to step over the output statement.
Press Shift+F5 to stop debugging.
Open App/Program.cs without changing the selected debug target.
Explain why pressing F5 at this moment may still start ScratchPad.
Remove the breakpoint with F9.
If the target selector behaves inconsistently, return to Run and Debug or use the explicit dotnet run --project command.

labs.title: Recover Through the Command Palette
labs.objective: Use command discovery to recover from forgotten shortcuts, RDP interception, hidden panels, and confusing layout state.
labs.task: Recover several common VS Code states by searching for commands instead of memorizing another set of shortcuts.
instructions: Press Ctrl+Shift+P.
Search for View: Toggle Primary Side Bar Visibility.
Run the matching command.
Open the Command Palette again.
Search for View: Single Column.
Run the matching command.
Open the Command Palette again.
Search for Format Document.
Notice the shortcut displayed beside the command in your installation.
Press Escape without running the format command again.
Open the Command Palette again.
Search for a command containing Select and Start Debugging.
Identify how you would use it to replace a stale debug target.
If RDP blocks a shortcut, repeat the action through the Command Palette.
Restore the sidebar, terminal, and one-column layout before finishing.

labs.title: Read a Dense Generic Signature
labs.objective: Translate Join's generic signature into the concrete Employee, WorkSummary, int, and string types used in Session 22.
labs.task: Use editor tooling to reconstruct the four-part Join call from its signature rather than recalling it from memory.
instructions: Open the Session 22 ClockEntryAnalytics.EmployeeLabels method.
Place the cursor immediately after the opening parenthesis in employees.Join(.
Press Ctrl+Shift+Space to open signature help.
If multiple overloads appear, use the signature-help arrows to inspect them without changing code.
Identify employees as the object on which Join is called; this is the first sequence, or TOuter.
Read the first displayed parameter as the second sequence and translate TInner to WorkSummary.
Read the next two parameters as key selectors and translate TKey to int because Identity and EmployeeId are integers.
Read the final selector as the result builder and translate TResult to string because EmployeeLabels returns labels.
Use the memory anchor: second collection, first key, second key, final result.
If signature help is too dense, press F12 on Join or open its official documentation, then return with Alt+Left.
Reconstruct the call one argument at a time and confirm IntelliSense advances to the next parameter after each comma.

lab.expectedBehavior: The learner can navigate and control the multi-project workspace, explicitly run ScratchPad, deliberately select a debug target, use a breakpoint, and recover common UI states without changing application behavior. The learner can also decode Join's signature by substituting concrete course types for generic placeholders.

commit: Not applicable — optional workflow lab; no source files should change.
review: No source or project file was intentionally changed.
Ctrl+P was used for file navigation rather than repeated Explorer browsing.
The learner can explain that F5 follows the selected debug configuration, not the visible file.
ScratchPad was run once with an explicit project path.
A breakpoint was added, reached, and removed.
Ctrl+Shift+P was used as a recovery path rather than treated as one more shortcut to memorize.
Join was reconstructed from signature help as second collection, first key, second key, and final result.

postQuiz.prompt: Why is Ctrl+Shift+P more important than memorizing every VS Code shortcut?
options: It lets you search for and execute commands by intent
postQuiz.explanation: The Command Palette is a discoverable fallback for forgotten, unbound, or intercepted commands.

postQuiz.prompt: You are viewing App/Program.cs, but ScratchPad is still selected in Run and Debug. What can F5 start?
options: Only App because its file is visible
postQuiz.explanation: The selected debug target is independent of the active editor and may persist from earlier work.

postQuiz.prompt: What is the safest response when an RDP session intercepts a shortcut?
options: Find and run the command through Ctrl+Shift+P
Assume VS Code removed the feature
postQuiz.explanation: The Command Palette avoids dependence on a particular key combination reaching the remote editor.

reflections: Which five commands would remove the most friction from your current workflow?
How will you verify the selected debug target before pressing F5 in a multi-project solution?
Which confusing VS Code states can you now recognize as reversible UI state rather than code problems?
whatBreaks: Skipping this optional sidebar does not break Session 02 or the TimeClock application. The cost is practical friction: slower navigation, more mouse dependence, and a greater chance of running or debugging a remembered project target unintentionally.
summary: Navigate to the file or symbol you need, manipulate reversible editor state, choose Run and Debug targets deliberately, and recover through Ctrl+Shift+P. A small command set plus an understanding of VS Code state is more useful than memorizing a giant shortcut list.
